paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: Suppose your university is seeking students’ opinions on the necessity of making College Chinese a compulsory course. You are now to write an essay to express your view. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：假设你的大学正在征求学生对将大学语文列为必修课的必要性的意见。你现在要写一篇文章来表达你的观点。你将有 30 分钟的时间来写这篇文章。您应该写至少 120 个字但不超过 180 个字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you will hear three news reports. At the end of each news report, you will hear two or three questions. Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D. Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.

paragraphs.sourceText: Sir Alfred Hitchcock was an English movie director and producer. Famously 26 to as ‘The Master of Suspense,’ Hitchcock is one of the most influential filmmakers in the history of 27 . He was an extraordinary director who entertained his audience with 28 and gripping suspense movies.
paragraphs.translationZh: 阿尔弗雷德·希区柯克爵士是一位英国电影导演和制片人。希区柯克被誉为“悬念大师”，是电影史上最有影响力的电影制片人之一。他是一位非凡的导演，以引人入胜、扣人心弦的悬疑电影取悦观众。

paragraphs.sourceText: His fascination with crime began at an early age when he was 29 by his father who made him spend a few minutes inside a prison for his misconduct. Hence, his movies are 30 of the guilt and innocence of the wrongdoer and the victim. He had a gift for creating stories that consisted of deceit, robbery, murder, corruption, and other criminal 31 with incredible plot twists in the storyline. The principal characters in his movies were often ordinary people 32 in unwanted and unavoidable situations.
paragraphs.translationZh: 他对犯罪的迷恋从很小的时候就开始了，当时他因行为不当而受到父亲的惩罚，父亲让他在监狱里呆了几分钟。因此，他的电影象征着加害者和受害者的有罪和清白。他有创作故事的天赋，其中包括欺骗、抢劫、谋杀、腐败和其他刑事犯罪，故事情节曲折得令人难以置信。他的电影中的主要角色通常是陷入不受欢迎和不可避免的境地的普通人。

paragraphs.sourceText: He was 33 productive and his amazing body of work is considered fascinating by the critics. Most of his movies have 34 the test of time and are considered to be masterpieces. He is also remembered by other filmmakers, for he continues to inspire them to be passionate about their work. He is also 35 by people around the world for his entertaining and exciting stories.
paragraphs.translationZh: 他的作品非常多产，评论家认为他的作品令人着迷。他的大部分电影都经受住了时间的考验，被认为是杰作。他也被其他电影制作人所铭记，因为他不断激励他们对工作充满热情。他还因其有趣而激动人心的故事而受到世界各地人们的崇拜。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: Is juicing actually good for you?
paragraphs.translationZh: 榨汁真的对你有好处吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Freshly juiced fruit has become a basic dietary item — especially for busy, health-conscious consumers who can save time on making (and perhaps even chewing) their food without missing out on nutrients. Fruit juice also has been linked to claims that it can help you both lose weight and stay healthy. All of which, of course, has made it highly profitable. The global fruit and vegetable juices market was valued at $154 billion in 2016 and is expected to grow.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 鲜榨果汁已成为一种基本饮食项目，尤其是对于忙碌、注重健康的消费者来说，他们可以节省制作（甚至咀嚼）食物的时间，而不会错过营养。果汁还被认为可以帮助减肥和保持健康。当然，所有这些都使其获得了高额利润。 2016 年全球果蔬汁市场价值 1540 亿美元，预计还将增长。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) But is juicing really as healthy as we think? Most foods containing fructose — a naturally occurring sugar found in all fruits and fruit juices — don’t seem to have harmful effects as long as they’re not contributing to excess daily calories. This is because the fibre found in whole fruits is intact, and the sugar is contained within the fruit’s cells. It takes our digestive system a while to break these cells down and for fructose to enter the bloodstream.
paragraphs.translationZh: B）但是榨汁真的像我们想象的那么健康吗？大多数含有果糖的食物（一种存在于所有水果和果汁中的天然糖）只要不导致每日卡路里摄入过多，似乎就不会产生有害影响。这是因为整个水果中的纤维是完整的，并且糖包含在水果的细胞内。我们的消化系统需要一段时间才能分解这些细胞并使果糖进入血液。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) But this is not the case with fruit juice. Unlike whole fruit, fruit juice has most of the fibre removed. This is why the fructose in fruit juices counts as “free sugars” — which also include honey and the sugars added to foods. It’s recommended by the World Health Organisation that adults have no more than 30g of added sugar, the equivalent of 150ml of fruit juice, per day. The problem is that, with the fibre removed, fruit juice’s fructose is absorbed more quickly. Sudden increases in blood sugar cause the release of insulin (胰岛素) to bring it back down to a stable level. Over time, this mechanism can wear out, increasing the risk of developing type 2 diabetes. In 2013, researchers analysed the health data of 100,000 people collected between 1986 and 2009 and found that fruit juice consumption was linked with increased risk of type 2 diabetes. Another study found a relationship between fruit juice and type 2 diabetes after following the diets and diabetes status of more than 70,000 nurses over 18 years. The researchers explain that the possible reason for this may partly have been the lack of the other components found in whole fruit, like fibre.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 但果汁则不然。与整个水果不同，果汁去除了大部分纤维。这就是为什么果汁中的果糖被视为“游离糖”——其中还包括蜂蜜和添加到食物中的糖。世界卫生组织建议成人每天添加糖分不超过30克，相当于150毫升果汁。问题是，随着纤维的去除，果汁中的果糖会被更快地吸收。血糖突然升高会导致胰岛素（胰岛素）的释放，使其恢复到稳定水平。随着时间的推移，这种机制会逐渐失效，从而增加患 2 型糖尿病的风险。 2013年，研究人员分析了1986年至2009年间收集的10万人的健康数据，发现饮用果汁与2型糖尿病风险增加有关。另一项研究在 18 年来跟踪了 70,000 多名护士的饮食和糖尿病状况后发现了果汁与 2 型糖尿病之间的关系。研究人员解释说，造成这种情况的部分原因可能是整个水果中缺乏纤维等其他成分。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Juices containing vegetables can provide more nutrients and less sugar than juices made up of just fruit — but they still lack valuable fibre. Diets high in fibre have been linked to a lower risk of developing heart disease, stroke, high blood pressure and diabetes, and it’s recommended adults consume 30g per day.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 与仅由水果组成的果汁相比，含有蔬菜的果汁可以提供更多的营养和更少的糖——但它们仍然缺乏有价值的纤维。高纤维饮食可降低患心脏病、中风、高血压和糖尿病的风险，建议成年人每天摄入 30 克纤维。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Aside from the link to type 2 diabetes, many studies agree that fruit juice is harmful if it contributes to an excess in calories. In an analysis of 155 studies, John Sievenpiper, associate professor at the University of Toronto’s Department of Nutritional Sciences, set out to understand if the associations between sugary soft drinks and health — including risk of diabetes and heart disease — were applicable to the food and drink we generally consume as part of a healthy diet. He compared studies looking into the effects of fructose-containing sugars with control diets free from or lower in these sugars. His aim? To isolate the effects of consuming too many calories from the effects of foods containing different sugars.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 除了与 2 型糖尿病的关联之外，许多研究都认为，如果果汁会导致热量过剩，那么它也是有害的。多伦多大学营养科学系副教授 John Sievenpiper 在对 155 项研究进行分析后，着手了解含糖软饮料与健康（包括患糖尿病和心脏病的风险）之间的关联是否适用于我们通常作为健康饮食一部分而消费的食物和饮料。他将含果糖的影响研究与不含或含果糖含量较低的对照饮食进行了比较。他的目的是什么？将摄入过多卡路里的影响与含有不同糖分的食物的影响分开。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) He found negative effects on blood sugar and insulin levels when food provided excess calories from sugars, including fruit juice. However, when the calories weren’t in excess overall, there were some advantages to consuming whole fruit — and even fruit juice. Sievenpiper concludes that the recommended 150ml of fruit juice per day, which is an average serving, is reasonable. The paper concluded that foods containing fructose may have some small benefits for long-term blood sugar control when they don’t lead to over-consumption of calories. But when they do lead to too many calories, they risk raising blood sugar and insulin levels.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 他发现，当食物（包括果汁）从糖中提供过量热量时，会对血糖和胰岛素水平产生负面影响。然而，当热量总体不过剩时，食用整个水果甚至果汁都有一些好处。 Sievenpiper 得出的结论是，每天推荐的 150 毫升果汁（即平均份量）是合理的。该论文的结论是，含有果糖的食物在不会导致卡路里过度消耗的情况下，可能对长期血糖控制有一些小好处。但当它们确实导致摄入过多热量时，就有升高血糖和胰岛素水平的风险。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) So while we know that fruit juice can cause diabetes if it’s part of a diet that has more calories overall, it’s less clear how juice affects the long-term health of those who aren’t overweight. But we have a higher risk of consuming more than the recommended daily number of calories (around 2,000 for women and 2,500 for men) on the days we drink juice, according to research. Numerous studies have shown that drinking fruit juice doesn’t make us consume any less of other foods throughout the day.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 因此，虽然我们知道，如果果汁是总体卡路里含量较高的饮食的一部分，果汁可能会导致糖尿病，但目前还不清楚果汁如何影响那些不超重的人的长期健康。但研究表明，在喝果汁的日子里，我们摄入的热量超过每日推荐热量（女性约 2,000 卡路里，男性约 2,500 卡路里）的风险更高。大量研究表明，喝果汁并不会让我们一天中摄入的其他食物减少。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) As it is easy to consume large amounts of fruit juice quite quickly, extra calories are taken in. And extra calories can contribute to weight gain. One way we can improve the effects of fruit juice on our health is making sure we select ripe fruit to retain as much of its goodness as possible, according to Roger Clemens, professor of pharmaceutical (药物的) sciences at the University of Southern California.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 由于很容易很快消耗大量果汁，因此会摄入额外的热量。而额外的热量会导致体重增加。南加州大学药物科学教授罗杰·克莱门斯 (Roger Clemens) 表示，改善果汁对健康影响的一种方法是确保选择成熟的水果，以尽可能保留其优点。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Another reason for fruit juice’s recent popularity is the argument that it can help to remove poisonous or harmful substances from the body. However, “the whole concept of a juice diet helping to remove poisonous or harmful substances from the body is completely false,” says Clemens. “We consume compounds every day that may be poisonous and our bodies do a wonderful job of removing and eliminating anything harmful from our bodies.”
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 果汁最近流行的另一个原因是它可以帮助清除体内有毒或有害物质。然而，“果汁饮食有助于清除体内有毒或有害物质的整个概念是完全错误的，”克莱门斯说。 “我们每天都会摄入可能有毒的化合物，而我们的身体在清除和消除体内任何有害物质方面做得非常出色。”

paragraphs.sourceText: J) And juice isn’t a cure-all for getting your nutrients, either. “There are a lot of nutrients contained in the parts of the fruits, such as in apple skins, that are excluded when you juice them,” says Heather Ferris, a professor of medicine. “You end up with sugary water with some vitamins.”
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 果汁也不是获取营养的万能药。医学教授希瑟·费里斯 (Heather Ferris) 表示：“水果的各个部分（例如苹果皮）中含有大量营养成分，但在榨汁时这些营养成分会被排除。” “你最终会得到含有一些维生素的糖水。”

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Plus. she adds, it’s not an ideal way to reach the advised ‘five a day’. “People try to get five servings of fruit and vegetables per day and don’t realise this isn’t just about getting vitamins,” she says. “It’s also about reducing the amount of grain carbs (碳水化合物) and protein and fats in our diet, and increasing fibre.” So while fruit juice is better than no fruit at all, there are limits. It particularly comes with risks when we consume more than 150ml of free sugars per day, or when it puts us over our recommended calorie intake. It provides us with vitamins — but fruit juice is far from a quick fix.
paragraphs.translationZh: K）加上。她补充道，这并不是达到建议的“每天五次”的理想方式。 “人们试图每天摄入五份水果和蔬菜，但没有意识到这不仅仅是获取维生素，”她说。 “这还涉及减少饮食中碳水化合物、蛋白质和脂肪的含量，并增加纤维。”因此，虽然果汁比没有水果好，但也有局限性。当我们每天摄入超过 150 毫升的游离糖，或者超过我们建议的卡路里摄入量时，尤其会带来风险。它为我们提供维生素，但果汁远非快速解决问题的办法。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Fruit juice is different from whole fruit in that it contains much less fibre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 果汁与整个水果不同，它含有的纤维要少得多。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Some people believe a juice diet helps to rid our body of harmful or poisonous substances.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 有些人认为果汁饮食有助于清除体内有害或有毒物质。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. A lot of research comes to the same conclusion that fruit juice does harm to the human body when it leads to surplus calories.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 很多研究都得出同样的结论：果汁导致热量过剩，对人体有害。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. The claimed health benefits of fruit and vegetable juices have rendered the industry very profitable.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 声称的果汁和蔬菜汁对健康有益，使该行业利润丰厚。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. To increase the benefits of fruit juice to our health, we’d better choose ripe fruit to make juice.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40.为了增加果汁对我们健康的益处，我们最好选择成熟的水果来制作果汁。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Diets containing large amounts of fibre reduce the risk of heart disease, diabetes and other health hazards.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 含有大量纤维的饮食可降低患心脏病、糖尿病和其他健康危害的风险。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. According to a research paper, drinking fruit juice is beneficial on condition that it is consumed in reasonable amounts.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 根据一项研究论文，饮用果汁是有益的，但前提是适量饮用。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. One expert claims that juicing wastes a lot of nutrients contained in fruits.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 一位专家声称，榨汁浪费了水果中含有的大量营养成分。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. It takes some time for fruit’s cells to be digested and for fructose to be absorbed.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 水果细胞被消化和果糖被吸收需要一些时间。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. A lot of research has demonstrated that drinking fruit juice does not reduce our daily consumption of other foods.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 很多研究表明，喝果汁并不会减少我们日常摄入的其他食物。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A, B, C and D. You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A、B、C 和 D。您应该决定最佳选项，并在答题纸 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: We all take a little extra effort to look nice for special occasions. But most of us have conflicting feelings about dressing up and feel guilty about taking the time to focus on clothes. Science now suggests the right dress may give ourselves the extra edge in our professional and personal lives.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们都会付出一些额外的努力，让自己在特殊场合看起来漂亮。但我们大多数人对着装都有矛盾的感觉，并且对花时间关注衣服感到内疚。现在的科学表明，合适的着装可能会给我们的职业和个人生活带来额外的优势。

paragraphs.sourceText: We hear sayings like “dress for the job you want; not the job you have”. Most people don’t really believe in them, but research into the impact of clothes on behavior now suggests that there may actually be a grain of truth in these sayings. Science says that the clothes we wear affect our behavior, our mood and even the way we interact with others because of the symbolic meaning that we assign to different types of clothing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们听到这样的说法：“为你想要的工作着装，而不是你现有的工作”。大多数人并不真正相信这些说法，但现在对服装对行为影响的研究表明，这些说法实际上可能有一定道理。科学表明，我们穿的衣服会影响我们的行为、情绪，甚至我们与他人互动的方式，因为我们赋予不同类型的衣服不同的象征意义。

paragraphs.sourceText: We consider some clothes to be powerful, some to be fun, and so on. We even evaluate people whom we have just met based on their clothes. We also evaluate ourselves based on what we are wearing because of the way they make us feel. This means that the experience of wearing something affects our attitudes and our choice of behavior.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们认为有些衣服很强大，有些很有趣，等等。我们甚至根据衣着来评价刚认识的人。我们还会根据我们的穿着来评估自己，因为它们给我们带来的感觉。这意味着穿着体验会影响我们的态度和行为选择。

paragraphs.sourceText: There’s a reason tailored jackets are associated with being ‘dressed for success’. It seems that wearing formal office wear puts us in the right frame of mind to conduct business. Wearing power clothing makes us feel more confident and even increases hormones needed for displaying dominance. This in turn helps us become better negotiators and abstract thinkers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 定制夹克与“成功着装”联系在一起是有原因的。穿着正式的办公服装似乎能让我们以正确的心态开展业务。穿着权力服装让我们感觉更加自信，甚至会增加展现统治力所需的荷尔蒙。这反过来又帮助我们成为更好的谈判者和抽象思考者。

paragraphs.sourceText: While a good suit works wonders for our performance in the boardroom, wearing formal wear isn’t a great idea when we want to socialize. Studies have found that people tend to be less open and less able to relax when they wear formal clothes.
paragraphs.translationZh: 虽然一套好的西装可以为我们在董事会中的表现带来奇迹，但当我们想要社交时，穿正装并不是一个好主意。研究发现，人们在穿正式服装时往往不太开放，也不太能够放松。

paragraphs.sourceText: On the other hand, a casual dress helps us become more friendly and creative. These findings support the idea of wearing business casuals on a Friday; since colleagues are most likely to take out time to socialize on the last work day of the week. I mean, who wants to hang out with people in their suits?
paragraphs.translationZh: 另一方面，休闲着装可以帮助我们变得更加友好和富有创造力。这些发现支持周五穿商务休闲装的想法；因为同事们最有可能在一周的最后一个工作日抽出时间进行社交活动。我的意思是，谁愿意和穿着西装的人一起出去玩呢？

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: With the rise of pop music, jazz, and electronic music, both opera and classical music started to fade away from the public eye. Some people are beginning to wonder whether opera and classical music are still relevant to the modern world of music. Granted, you will not typically see today’s teenagers lending their ears to Bach anytime soon, but there are some major indicators that both opera and classical music are now still quite alive.
paragraphs.translationZh: 随着流行音乐、爵士乐和电子音乐的兴起，歌剧和古典音乐开始淡出公众的视线。有些人开始怀疑歌剧和古典音乐是否仍然与现代音乐世界相关。诚然，你通常不会很快看到今天的青少年聆听巴赫的音乐，但有一些主要迹象表明歌剧和古典音乐现在仍然很活跃。

paragraphs.sourceText: The most major indicator of classical music’s importance in society today is the fact that much of the popular music that is currently being produced uses similar beats, harmonies, and melodies (旋律) as those that were used in some of classical music’s best works. Even so, it can be difficult for those who do not study music theory to see this as an indicator, since it is subtle and just shows the impact symphonic (交响乐的) orchestras have had on society’s taste in music.
paragraphs.translationZh: 古典音乐在当今社会中的重要性的最重要标志是，目前正在制作的许多流行音乐都使用与一些古典音乐最佳作品中使用的相似的节拍、和声和旋律（旋律）。即便如此，对于那些不学音乐理论的人来说，很难将其视为一个指标，因为它很微妙，只是显示了交响乐团对社会音乐品味的影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: A better example for the relevance of opera and classical music can be seen in the invention of the rock opera. Opera, in its simplest definition, is telling a story using music as its form. The art of telling a story using music has not faded in the least bit. In fact, sometimes actual orchestras are used for major parts of the opera itself. Some of the world’s greatest hits have been parts of rock operas.
paragraphs.translationZh: 摇滚歌剧的发明是歌剧和古典音乐相关性的一个更好的例子。歌剧，用最简单的定义来说，就是用音乐作为形式讲述故事。用音乐讲故事的艺术丝毫没有消失。事实上，有时歌剧本身的主要部分会使用真正的管弦乐队。世界上一些最热门的歌曲都是摇滚歌剧的一部分。

paragraphs.sourceText: Fans of classical music can also tell you that there are few types of music that are more expressive. So, it should come as no surprise to anyone that classical music pieces are still used as background music in modern movies. Symphonic orchestra compositions have also been created solely for the purpose of being included in major motion pictures. These are often very well received amongst mainstream music fans.
paragraphs.translationZh: 古典音乐爱好者还可以告诉你，很少有类型的音乐更具表现力。因此，古典音乐作品仍然被用作现代电影的背景音乐，这对任何人来说都不足为奇。交响乐团的作品也只是为了出现在主要电影中而创作的。这些通常受到主流音乐迷的欢迎。

paragraphs.sourceText: Classical music and opera are the very foundation of what our modern music is based upon. Considering the huge impact they have had on our current society, it is without doubt that we can expect them to continue to remain important for centuries to come.
paragraphs.translationZh: 古典音乐和歌剧是我们现代音乐的基础。考虑到它们对我们当前社会产生的巨大影响，毫无疑问，我们可以期望它们在未来几个世纪中继续保持重要地位。
